description: v0.4 candidate: how a host interprets the command field requested_by. Each case is a scenario, not signed bytes: build it on a fresh host with one company whose controller is "owner", a second registered person "member" who is an active member, a third registered person "outsider" who is not a member, and, for installation cases, one installation created by the owner (so the owner is its sponsor) with the given mode. A case with sponsor "member" instead invites the member with the permission installations.manage and has the member create the installation (so the member is its sponsor); with sponsor_revoked true, the owner then revokes the sponsor's membership (membership.revoke) before the case's command. Sign the command with the actor's key, plus the key of each person listed in co_signers. A host must give the expected outcome: "accept", or a refusal with the given error code and HTTP status. A host that accepts a refused case, refuses an accepted one, or refuses with another code, is non-conforming. The rule is in spec/v0.4/SPEC.md section 2 (Requester).
rule: Person actor: requested_by MUST equal actor.id (person.register included). Installation actor: requested_by null is an autonomous call, allowed only when the installation's mode is "automation" and its sponsor is still an active member; a non-null requested_by is an interactive call, allowed in either mode, only when it names an active member of the company who also signs the command. A non-null requested_by never falls back to the autonomous path.
